references.text: The psalmist describes directly how the king sent word and released Joseph, setting him as ruler over his house – a poetic rendering of Gen 41:14.
Joseph himself refers to his imprisonment as a 'bor' (cistern/well), which provides the background for the expression that they hurried him out from the 'well' in 41:14.
King Jehoiachin changed his prison garments and ate at the king's table in Babylon, paralleling Joseph who shaved himself and changed clothes before appearing before Pharaoh.
Daniel was brought quickly before King Nebuchadnezzar to interpret the king's dream, a direct parallel to Joseph being taken from prison to interpret Pharaoh's dreams.
Joseph was thrown into prison, which provides the direct context for his release and exaltation in 41:14.
Both verses document the same transition ritual (changing of clothes/symbols) that marks Joseph's complete elevation from prisoner to second-in-command of Egypt.
Both verses document the same historical moment: Joseph's appearance before Pharaoh, marking his transition from prisoner to second-in-command of Egypt.
